Sentence (English): Reason for Purchase: As the number of children's dishes increased, I found myself washing them several times a day, which was time-consuming and exhausting.
Comments (English): Reason for Purchase: As the number of children's dishes increased, I found myself washing them several times a day, which was time-consuming and exhausting. I felt a dishwasher was essential, so after comparing various models, I purchased the LG DIOS because of the many positive reviews regarding its cleaning power and True Steam function. Since this is an appliance I plan to use for a long time, I chose LG, a brand I can trust. Appearance: The Nature Beige color is truly beautiful. I liked it in photos, but seeing it installed in person, the color looks much more luxurious and subtle, completely transforming the atmosphere of my kitchen. Being a built-in unit, it blends in neatly and seems to add to the interior decor. Installation Process: The technician visited at the scheduled time and carried out the installation meticulously. They kindly explained how to use and maintain the appliance, so even a first-time user could operate it immediately without difficulty. I was also satisfied with the clean finish. Cleaning Power: The cleaning power is truly beyond my expectations. It cleans dishes with rice grains or grease, and I was surprised at how well pots and pans were cleaned as well as I thought. Since it is a 14-place setting capacity, there is plenty of room for dishes, making it very convenient to handle everything at once. I feel even more at ease using it because the True Steam function allows for sterilization of children's dishes. The noise level isn't high, so you can run it at night without any worries. Overall Impression: After using it myself, I understood why dishwashers are called "quality-of-life appliances." As the time spent washing dishes decreased, I was able to spend more time with my children, and my day felt much more relaxed. Since the design, cleaning power, and convenience were all satisfactory, I didn't feel at all that the price was wasted. I confidently recommend this product to families with children like mine, or to anyone looking to reduce dishwashing stress. It was a purchase I deliberated over for a long time, and I am truly satisfied with it.

Sentence (English): I used to use a 6-place setting dishwasher, but there wasn't enough space to fit all of my family's dishes at once, so I always had to be very careful about arranging them.
Comments (English): [ Switching from a 6-person to a 14-person set has changed my quality of life! ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-place setting dishwasher, but there wasn't enough space to fit all of my family's dishes at once, so I always had to be very careful about arranging them. Since switching to the LG DIOS Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in model, that worry has completely disappeared. What I like most is the three-tier shelf structure. The top shelf allows for neat organization of cutlery and cooking utensils, while the middle shelf can comfortably hold small plates, cups, and rice bowls. The bottom shelf is deep, making it incredibly convenient to fit not only large plates but also pots, pans, and knives all at once. Since it is a 14-place setting, there is ample space, so I rarely get stressed about arranging dishes, and washing dishes has become much easier. In the past, I used to run multiple cycles or worry about where to put them, but now I can handle most things in one go. I am satisfied with the cleaning power, and dishes are finished so clean that I rarely need to wash them by hand anymore. As it is a built-in model, it blends naturally with the kitchen, and the Objet Collection design is sleek, which has even increased my satisfaction with the interior. If you are considering replacing your dishwasher, I highly recommend the 14-place setting model over the 6-place setting. It is a highly satisfying product, so much so that once you use it, you will immediately understand why choosing a larger capacity is worthwhile. Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. Even though an acquaintance highly recommended their 6-place setting dishwasher, I wasn't interested because I'm an impatient person who needs to wash and tidy up immediately after cooking to feel at ease. As a working couple, washing a single dish after dinner is such a chore and a hassle; it leads to a game of "who does it" and "who does it." Even washing dishes from a simple dinner takes at least 30 minutes. While visiting my acquaintance's house, I saw the dishwasher they had been recommending so much and really wanted it. However, I hesitated again because I didn't like the design. Since I've always chanted "Samsung for appliances, Samsung for design, Samsung for stock" (Samsung Electronics), I searched for a Samsung model and thought, "Aha!" The design was perfect, too. So, I bought it online at a great price. At first, thinking detergent was a waste of money, I only used it when there was a lot of dishes. But as they say, once you stand, you want to sit, and once you sit, you want to lie down. After experiencing the convenience of a dishwasher once or twice, I now only do the dishes briefly for the kids' breakfast. It is so convenient, and I am so grateful to the person who invented it for having such a modern gadget in a capitalist society. I am also very grateful to my husband for buying it for me without a word of complaint. With two sons who are big eaters and a family that cooks at home, it is enough to wash everything for a single meal all at once. If I forget some cutlery or dishes while washing, I just press a "Stop!" button and add them to the cycle. It is that convenient. Just buy it. Hesitating only increases housewife's eczema.

Comments (English): [ Thermal Fuse - Buyer Beware ] || ---------------- || Less than 3 months in and the Thermal Fuse blew. So it's DOA and no power. This is a known concern with KitchenAid dishwasher. The problem? Even if you replace the thermal fuse you still have to figure out what caused the fuse to blow? Something causes it to blow. So a technician will come out, diagnose the fuse blew, replace the fuse and then hope and pray it was just a bad fuse. Because otherwise it will be dumb luck finding what is blowing the fuse. If it blows right away, the technician can't find what is blowing it. If it runs, unless something heats up right away, there is nothing the repair technician can do. It's fixed and runs. until the part that caused the fuse to blow engages again. It could be the 1 hour wash that causes it to blow? It could be the sanitize dry with the ProWash setting? It could be. and the list goes on. So until you can find the part causing the thermal fuse to blow you will be constantly calling out a technician. And the technician will just have to start replacing their best guess on which part is causing the issue. Which means you will not have a dishwasher each time. Stay away.

Sentence (English): **Review of the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-Place capacity) White**.
Comments (English): **Review of the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-Place Capacity) White**. Through the recent Samsung Appreciation Festival, I had the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-Place Capacity) installed, and after using it, I understand why so many people recommend it. The most satisfying aspect is the generous 14-place capacity. For a family of three, it was incredibly convenient to be able to fit all the dishes, pots, and pans from the day in one go, eliminating the need for multiple washes. The cleaning performance is also very satisfactory. Even greasy pans and dishes stained with sauce were cleaned thoroughly, and water stains on cups and glassware were significantly reduced. I particularly liked that the hot air drying function dried the dishes almost perfectly after use, eliminating the need to wipe them dry separately. The AI features were also more useful than I expected. Since it recommends a course based on the volume and soiling level of the dishes, I didn't have to worry about which mode to select. Additionally, it was convenient to be able to check the operation status or receive completion notifications by connecting it to my smartphone. In addition, the built-in design made the kitchen look much cleaner and more integrated, resulting in high satisfaction with the interior. The white color blends well with any kitchen, creating a luxurious atmosphere. Above all, the noise level was lower than expected, allowing me to use it without worry even in the evenings or after my child had gone to sleep. I believe the biggest advantage is that it saves time on dishwashing, allowing me to spend more time with my family. Sentence (English): Review of the LG DIOS Objet Collection Dishwasher (Freestanding/14-Place capacity).

Being able to wash everything at once—from children's dishes to pots and pans—has made my daily routine much easier. I am particularly satisfied because it cleans even greasy dishes and those with stuck-on rice residue. The Objet design is clean and blends well with my kitchen decor, and having used it every day, it has now become an indispensable appliance. Overall: This is a product that will satisfy any household looking to reduce dishwashing time. I am satisfied with the cleaning power, drying performance, and quietness. I believe it is an appliance that definitely improves the quality of life, especially for dual-income couples or families with children.

Sentence (English): This is a Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher I purchased to install at my parents' house.
Comments (English): This is a Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher I purchased to install at my parents' house. At first, I was very worried about whether it would fit because the sink area is narrow. However, since countertop extension plates are available separately these days, I purchased one along with the dishwasher and installed it, and it fit perfectly and neatly, much better than I expected. If you are concerned about space, I recommend looking into the extension plate as well. My parents are highly satisfied, having used it for a few days, to the point where they asked, "Why did we wait so long to buy this?" They particularly mentioned how convenient it is to run the machine immediately without having to wash by hand, even when there is only a small amount of dishes. As they get older, their wrists and backs tend to ache, but this definitely seems to reduce that strain. The cleaning power is also satisfactory. It cleans everyday rice bowls, soup bowls, and cups perfectly, and since it dries the dishes, there is almost no need to wipe them dry. The noise level is also quieter than expected, so I didn't really notice if it was running. Pros: Excellent cleaning power, so most dishes are washed cleanly. Convenient because it dries, allowing for immediate cleanup. The noise level is not high. Installation is possible even in narrow sink areas by using the countertop extension plate. My parents were extremely satisfied. Cons: Since it is a 6-person capacity, it might be a bit lacking if you want to fit multiple large pots or pans. I highly recommend measuring the space before installation. Overall, it was a truly satisfying product, making it a great gift for my parents. Hearing them say their dishwashing stress has significantly decreased makes me feel proud. If you have been hesitating due to space limitations, I think it would be a good idea to consider installing it with the extension plate. Ultimately, we are completely satisfied! Sentence (English): One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back.
Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

날에는 강한 코스로 돌리고 있습니다. 앱 연동도 가능해서 익숙해지면 더 편하게 쓸 수 있을 것 같습니다.설치도 방문 설치로 진행돼서 큰 어려움은 없었습니다. 빌트인 제품이라 설치 공간이나 걸레받이 부분은 미리 확인해두는 게 좋을 것 같고, 기사님이 설치하면서 기본적인 사용 방법도 설명해주셔서 처음 사용하는 데 도움이 됐습니다.아쉬운 점을 굳이 꼽자면, 만족합니다. 설거지 시간이 줄어드는 것도 좋지만, 식사 후 싱크대에 그릇이 쌓여 있는 걸 보는 스트레스가 줄어든 게 제일 큽니다. 손설거지할 때보다 물을 계속 틀어두지 않아도 되고, 위생적으로도 더 안심되는 느낌입니다. 가격 때문에 고민했는데 막상 써보니 생활 만족도를 꽤 크게 올려주는 가전이라고 생각합니다.식기세척기 처음 구매하시는 분들도 14인용으로 Sentence (English): I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced.
Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

만족합니다. 설거지 시간이 줄어드는 것도 좋지만, 식사 후 싱크대에 그릇이 쌓여 있는 걸 보는 스트레스가 줄어든 게 제일 큽니다. 손설거지할 때보다 물을 계속 틀어두지 않아도 되고, 위생적으로도 더 안심되는 느낌입니다. 가격 때문에 고민했는데 막상 써보니 생활 만족도를 꽤 크게 올려주는 가전이라고 생각합니다.식기세척기 처음 구매하시는 분들도 14인용으로 Sentence (English): I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.
Comments (English): [ I am more satisfied than I expected, so I am leaving a long review. ] || ---------------- || One of the appliances I agonized over the most when moving was the dishwasher, but to start with the conclusion, I now understand why everyone says once you use one, you can't go back. I hesitated a bit at first because the price was on the higher side, but after using it for a few days, I am quite satisfied as the time and stress I used to spend on washing dishes every day have been drastically reduced. First of all, the design features a Nature Beige color that blends naturally into the kitchen without standing out. Since it was installed as a built-in unit, it doesn't feel like a separate appliance but fits neatly inside the cabinet, which looks great, and I also like the calm color tone characteristic of the Objet Collection. It looks even more luxurious in person than in photos, and the color fits well in a bright kitchen without looking too dark. I was worried that the 14-place setting might be too big or overwhelming, but after actually using it, it feels just right. In fact, I think I would have regretted buying a smaller capacity model. Since I can fit pots, pans, plates, cups, and cutlery all in one go, cleaning up after meals is much easier. I particularly love that I can fit a generous amount of dishes. Even for a household of one or two people, if you cook frequently or eat a lot at home, the 14-place setting is definitely more convenient. The cleaning power exceeds expectations. Even dishes with dried-on rice or greasy plates are cleaned surprisingly well, leaving a squeaky clean feeling compared to washing by hand. The difference is particularly noticeable in how clean cups and glasses come out. Previously, I was bothered by water stains remaining on the inside of cups or the rims of plates, but after running the dishwasher, it feels like everything is cleaned evenly, which is great. The burden of washing dishes has been significantly reduced, even on days when I eat greasy food. The drying is also better than expected. While some water droplets may remain depending on the material, regular plates and glass cups dry quite well. I like that the door opens automatically to let moisture escape, and thanks to the hot air drying function, the finish is much cleaner than what I expected from a dishwasher. However, water sometimes pools slightly at the bottom of plastic containers or concave dishes, so users will need to carefully adjust the loading direction for this. The noise level is quieter than expected. It is not completely silent, but it is not bothersome; it feels about the same as the sound of running water in the kitchen. I don't think it would be too much of a burden to run it at night. It is not quiet enough to make you forget it is running, but it blends naturally into everyday noise. Rather than saying the controls are very intuitive, you need a little time to get used to the menus at first. Since there are various buttons and cycles, it is recommended to consult the manual when using it for the first time. However, after using it a few times, you will find that you use the cycles frequently, so it is not difficult. I mainly use the Standard or Automatic cycles, and on days with heavy soiling, I run the Strong cycle. It also supports app integration, so I think it will be even more convenient to use once you get used to it. Installation was done by a professional technician, so there were no major difficulties. Since it is a built-in product, it is a good idea to check the installation space and baseboards in advance, and the technician explained the basic usage methods during installation, which was helpful for first-time users. If I had to point out a drawback, washing or drying may not be perfect if you put the dishes in haphazardly, so you need to pay a little attention to dish placement at first. Also, the control menus do not feel very simple from the start, so if your parents use it, they might need some explanation at the beginning. However, this is something you adapt to quickly after using it for a few days, so it is hard to consider it a major flaw. Overall, I am really satisfied. While it is nice to have less dishwashing time, the biggest benefit is the reduced stress of seeing dishes piled up in the sink after meals. I don't have to leave the water running continuously like I did when washing by hand, and I feel much more at ease regarding hygiene. I hesitated because of the price, but now that I’ve actually used it, I think it is an appliance that significantly improves my quality of life. I recommend going for the 14-place setting model for first-time dishwashers. It might look big at first, but having ample space is much more convenient in practice. I am satisfied with the design, cleaning power, drying, and storage, and I think those who cook frequently at home will particularly appreciate the difference. I have absolutely no regrets about my purchase and am using it well.

Sentence (English): If all you want to do is look at this dishwasher, it'll do.
Comments (English): [ Poorly built but looks great (eye roll) ] || ---------------- || If all you want to do is look at this dishwasher, it'll do. If you want to actually open the door and use it, you might run into problems. From the time I opened the door, I realized this would be a poorly built (very expensive) problem; however, I had my appliances (ALL Samsung (refrigerator, oven, microwave, dishwasher, washer and dryer) delivered and installed 3 days before I actually moved into my house. Because I discovered the issues with the dishwasher after the 48 hour mark, Lowe's could not help me so they referred me to Samsung. Samsung said the only thing they could do was send a representative to perform maintenance, but refund/replacement was not an option. When I opened the door, there was a broken roller on the top rack and the hinge on the door made a loud bang every time I closed the door. It's a poorly built dishwasher and you would think after furnishing 2 houses in the past 6 years with ALL Samsung appliances, I could get some other response besides, "I'm sorry sir, there's nothing else we can do for you." I even told them I would accept a cheaper, better built dishwasher and "eat the difference." I was not trying to be difficult; I just want a dishwasher that won't fall apart or start leaking and cause other damages.Working in the real estate industry gives me ample opportunity to advise all my clients and other realtors to choose appliances that are not Samsung.

It is poorly designed (not enough prongs on the bottom drawer to allow efficient loading of dishes) to the point that it holds much less than my old 24” Kenmore (RIP). I have a choice after having family over - load dishes and one serving dish in bottom and glasses in top and wait to do a second cycle of dessert and coffee cups and more cookware. The middle drawer has the annoying habit of sliding forward as soon as you put one object into it, constantly bumping you as you try to load the bottom drawer. I am not sure what the point is of the top drawer as it too holds so little. Yes it does a good job but I am running this dishwasher twice as much as my old one because of the limited space within it.

Sentence (English): I ordered from Coupang, and I liked that the delivery was fast and I could get it installed right on the date I wanted.
Comments (English): [ The essential dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I ordered from Coupang, and I liked that the delivery was fast and I could get it installed right on the date I wanted. The installer was punctual, installed it neatly, and kindly explained how to use it. I think I made the right choice selecting the largest size, the 14-place setting. Pots and pans fit in at once, and it is so convenient because I don't have to run it multiple times, even on days when I have a lot of dishes. I chose the white color, and it blends naturally with my kitchen, making it look so clean that it seems like it was always installed there. I am satisfied because it doesn't detract from the interior but actually gives it a more sophisticated feel. The automatic door opening feature is also great! Once the wash is finished, the door opens automatically to let the moisture escape, so it is convenient because I can leave it running while I go out or sleep. My old one didn't have this automatic door opening feature, so it was inconvenient having to leave the door open every time. I am satisfied with the cleaning power, and the drastic reduction in dishwashing time has completely changed my quality of life. If you are considering buying a dishwasher, I recommend purchasing a large capacity model.
Comments (Original): [ 필수 가전 식기세척기! ] || ---------------- || 쿠팡에서 주문했는데 배송도 빠르고 원하는 날짜에 바로 설치받을 수 있어서 좋았어요. 설치 기사님도 시간 약속 잘 지켜주시고 설치도 깔끔하게 해주시면서 사용법까지 친절하게 설명해주셨습니다.14인용으로 가장 큰 사이즈를 선택하길 정말 잘한 것 같아요. 냄비나 프라이팬까지 한 번에 들어가고 식기가 많이 나오는 날에도 여러 번 돌릴 필요가 없어서 너무 편합니다.화이트 컬러를 선택했는데 주방이랑 자연스럽게 잘 어울려서 마치 원래부터 설치되어 있던 것처럼 깔끔해 보여요. 인테리어를 해치지 않고 오히려 더 세련된 느낌이 들어 만족스럽습니다.자동 문열림 기능도 너무 좋아요! 세척이 끝나면 문이 알아서 열리면서 내부 습기가 빠져나가니까 돌려놓고 외출하거나 자도 되어서 편해요. 예전 거는 자동문열림 기능이 없어서 매번 문 열어놔야해서 불편했었거든요. 세척력도 만족스럽고 설거지 시간이 확 줄어서 삶의 질이 달라졌어요. 식기세척기 고민 중이라면 큰 용량으로 구매하는 걸 추천합니다.

Sentence (English): The DW works as described.
Comments (English): [ DW great! Help from Lowes & Bosch needs attention ] || ---------------- || The DW works as described. I would give 5 stars. Lowes help after the initial purchase, responding to issues with delivery and a missing part,earns 2 stars.Ease of Installation earned 1 star.TThus, the overall 2 star average.Lowes service before installation: The purchase was easy (of course). The delivery had hiccups. The delivery service contacted us and indicated they were not hauling away the old, even though it was on the receipt and paid for. I called Lowe's, and they had me call the delivery service to correct the issue. I see that as Lowe's responsibility. Ultimately,. the delivery guys were great and careful and did haul off the old one.The Installation was a 3-day event. We have installed 5 dishwashers over the past 20 years, so we had no reason to pay for installation. We are not even sure it could have been provided; online, it could not. So here is our experience.Electrical: The DW was placed into a home built in 2004. Homes did not have outlets behind the DW at that time. We were prepared for the hardwire connection, but instructions indicated it had to be the Bosch product, requiring we use a Bosch J-box. What the heck--so that required another trip to Lowes. (120 miles round trip).Waste line: The instructions want the waste line at 33" AFF or higher. Countertops are at 36", and when you allow for the blocking and countertop itself, creating that level of drop required new holes to be drilled in the cabinet that were not needed in the previous DW.Leveling: We leveled it, then moved it in. But it was not level.(The back leg dropped) We then had to remove the DW after we installed it and readjust the back leg. Watch out for the front rubber lip on the DW; it required the use of multiple spatulas and tools to release that seal from the side cabinets to get the DW back out. Missing part: We are missing the felt/fleece covering for the bottom front panel. I called Lowes. They sent me to the wrong phone number at Bosch. Bosch got me to the correct number. I was on hold for so long, I hung up and will try again. So Lowes, twice, did not solve the issues, but had the client call around to solve the issue.I would highly recommend the Bosch dishwasher itself. It is quiet (even without the fleece panel) and operates great. I find the third drawer annoying and would prefer a larger utensil unit, but it was not an option. The service from Lowes was less than anticipated, and getting help from Bosch to replace a missing part has yet to be resolved.

Sentence (English): I feel like I can't live without a dishwasher now.
Comments (English): [ A dishwasher is, of course, a must. ] || ---------------- || I feel like I can't live without a dishwasher now. Samsung happened to be giving away Onnuri gift certificates, so I quickly bought one. It's usable even without the automatic door opening, but it's still nice to have it. I cook frequently, and as a family of four, we generate a lot of dishes. I did try a 12-place setting model before; while bigger is always better, it was inconvenient having to bend over, so I just repurchased the 6-place setting model. Since I run it frequently and don't do the washing all at once, this actually suits me better. If I do it all at once, I often end up having to wash dishes again if a dish I need happens to be in the dishwasher. For diligent housewives who cook often and can't stand seeing dishes pile up, the 6-place setting model would be great for a quick and satisfying wash! Tablet detergent definitely has better cleaning power than liquid or powder types. When I first got the dishwasher installed, I ran it twice with both powder and liquid detergents, but the dishes didn't get cleaned well. I even tried adding rinse aid, but it still didn't clean, so I was disappointed thinking I had gotten a defective unit. However, after buying the tablet version and running it again, it cleans perfectly. I like that there is a foldable section inside, which makes it convenient for playing Tetris. Since there are blades on both the top and bottom, it cleans very well, and best of all, I like that you can add rinse, dry, and sanitize modes. Adding all the functions does make the cycle longer, so I recommend adding them when you have the spare time. Getting a dishwasher drastically reduces dishwashing time, so I highly recommend buying one! If you have back pain, I recommend the 6-place setting model over the 12-place setting, but if you like stacking items before running them, I recommend the 12-place setting model.
Comments (Original): [ 역시 식기세척기는 필수입니다. ] || ---------------- || 이제는 식기세척기 없으면 못 살 것 같아요ㅜㅠ삼성에서 마침 온누리 상품권도 준다해서 냉큼 바꿨어요.자동문열림이 없어도 쓸만은 한데 그래도 있는게 좋네요.요리도 자주하고 4인 가족이라 식기가 많이 나와요.예전에 12인용도 써보긴했는데 물론 거거익선이지만 허리 숙이고 불편하긴 해서 그냥 6인용으로 재구매했습니다.수시로 돌리고 설거지를 몰아서 안하니 오히려 이게 저한테는 맞는 것 같아요.몰아서 하다보면 가끔 필요한 식기가 식기세척기에 있으면 결국 다시 설거지하는 경우가 있거든요 ㅋㅋ부지런하고 요리 자주하고 쌓여있는 꼴을 못 보는 주부님은 6인용이 속 시원해서 좋을 것 같습니다!액체나 가루형보다는 타블렛 형태가 확실히 세정력이 좋아요.처음에 식기세척기 설치 받고 가루와 액체로 두번 다 돌렸다가 설거지 너무 안되서 린스도 넣어보고 했지만 세척이 안되서 뽑기를 제대로 못 했나싶어 실망했거든요ㅜ근데 타블렛으로 사서 다시 돌리니 완벽하게 세척이 되네요.내부에 접었다 폈다하는 부분이 있어서 테트리스할때 용이해서 좋아요.날개도 위, 아래 있다보니 세척이 잘 되고 무엇보다 헹굼과 건조, 살균 모드를 추가할 수 있다는게 마음에 듭니다.기능들을 다 추가하면 시간이 길긴해서 여유있을때 추가해요.식기세척기 들이면 설거지 시간이 확 줄어들어서 꼭 구입하세요!ㅎㅎ 허리 아프신 분들은 12인용보단 6인 추천드리고 쌓아놓고 돌리는걸 좋아하시면 12인용 추천해드려요^^
